title: Bounded run-lifetime adaptive representation registry
motivation: F-AHL30 showed repeated uncached rebuilds above the 32-entry cache limit. F-AHL31 measured mean representation payload near 4.64 kB and projected about 46-55 MB support-array payload for 10000 unique representations. A much larger but still bounded run-lifetime exact-key registry is therefore plausible without eviction.

repair.allocation: lazy allocation of registry entry storage on first use
repair.indexing: open addressing from the existing 64-bit fingerprint; linear probing only for collision resolution
repair.collision_authority: fingerprint selects candidate slot, but a cache hit requires unchanged full collision-safe exact-key equality

rationale.target_scale: comfortably exceeds a 10000-profile all-unique synthetic case while remaining finite
rationale.note: payload projection excludes key/descriptor metadata but remains well below a 128 MiB support-payload envelope in the observed characterization

stage1.workload: 10000 unique deterministic parameterizations, one request each

stage2.workload: second pass over the same 10000 exact keys

stage3.gate: the 16385th request succeeds via uncached fallback and registry entries remain exactly 16384

decision_rule: Retain only if all correctness/cache-accounting gates pass and memory remains bounded by the fixed 16384-entry registry plus per-entry adaptive payload. No application speed claim is made from this synthetic registry qualification.
